what_sql_is.summary: SQL asks organized data for results. Tables hold that data in rows and columns.

what_sql_means.title: SQL asks data questions
what_sql_means.bodyMarkdown:
SQL is a language for asking questions of organized data.

A **database** stores data so software can work with it consistently. SQL describes the result you want from that stored data.

You do not need to memorize database theory before writing queries. Start with one question: **what information do I need back?**

what_a_database_is.title: Tables organize the data
what_a_database_is.bodyMarkdown:
Most data you will query in this course is organized in **tables**.

- A **row** (or record) represents one item.
- A **column** (or field) represents one kind of value.
- The **table name** tells you which collection of records you are using.
- **Column names** tell you which values are available.

Before writing SQL, identify the table and the columns that answer the question. That is enough database structure for the lessons that follow.
